title: LANE: Label-Aware Noise Elimination for Fine-Grained Text Classification
claim: Examples with correct labels receive high weights while mislabeled ones receive low weights, so the learned weight separates clean from noisy data.
layout: 3 panels in a row, overlaid shaded density curves, red vs blue
description: Three side-by-side density-style line plots, labeled (a) RCV1, (b) Amazon Review and (c) SciHTC. Each plot has Weight (0 to 1) on the x-axis and Proportion on the y-axis. The y-axis is shared and labeled only on the left. Each panel overlays two shaded curves. The red curve is Incorrect examples. It has a tall peak near weight 0 and falls off toward 0.4 to 0.5. The blue curve is Correct examples. It has a broad hump around 0.5 to 0.7 and tails off toward 1. The two areas overlap in purple at low weights. A boxed legend sits at the top left of each plot, and light dashed grid lines run behind the curves. The eye goes first to the red spike at the left and the blue hump on the right. Together they show that the two groups separate cleanly.
caption: Distribution of Correct and Incorrect Examples by Weight
abstract: In this paper, we propose Label-Aware Noise Elimination (LANE), a new approach to learning with noisy labels. At its core, LANE introduces a new metric---label-aware margin---aimed at quantifying the degree of noise of each training example (or quality thereof). LANE leverages the semantic relations between classes and monitors the training dynamics of the model on each training example to dynamically lower the weight of training examples that are perceived to have noisy labels. We test the effectiveness of LANE on multiple text classification tasks and benchmark our approach on a wide variety of datasets with various numbers of classes and amounts of label noise. LANE considerably outperforms strong baselines on all datasets and settings, obtaining significant improvements ranging from an average improvement of 2.88% in F1 on manually annotated datasets to a considerable average improvement of 4.75% F1 on datasets with high level of injected label noise. We carry out a comprehensive analysis of LANE and identify the key components that lead to its success.
